messages:
Oncall-Bot: ALERT: p99 latency breach on /v1/generate (hosted-us-east) — current p99 2.8s (SLO 1.5s). Auto-escalation: paging oncall @alex and @marta.
Alex: ack. I’m on it, moving to this thread. Any recent deploys? :eyes:
Priya: saw a small configservice deploy ~5m ago from ci/cd, but no model changes.
Marta: I'm watching metrics — tail latency spike correlates with control-plane errors from config-fetch (503s).
Jamal: customer-reported streaming stalls too (multiple support tickets). Nina, can you paste a customer example?
Nina: pasted sample logs from customer 'acme-pay': streaming connection opened then no tokens for ~10s, client saw spinner.
Alex: thanks. Initial hypothesis: config-fetch/featureflag checks are blocking inference path at request start for some traffic patterns.
Taylor: infra logs show increased auth token DB latency around the same time (rds-primary p95 150ms -> 800ms). Could be db connection pool exhaustion.
Infra-Bot: rds-primary CPU 68%, connections 980/1000, circuit-breakers tripped on some controlplane pods.
Priya: running a quick query on configservice traces. Traces show configservice waiting on tokenstore auth validation because of a burst of renewals.
Marta: timeline: 14:03 alert, 14:05 p95 climbed to 600ms, 14:08 p99 spike to 2.8s. Correlated with rollout of featureflag-service that has a new global evaluation path.
Jamal: can we route traffic away from the featureflag evaluation? Is there a simple bypass?
Alex: yes — featureflag has an env var FF_EVAL_SYNC=true vs false. If we set to false it will fallback to cached flags for 60s. That should remove control-plane dependency for flag checks.
Taylor: creating a canary config patch to set FF_EVAL_SYNC=false for hosted-us-east configservice pods.
Deploy-Bot: Deploying config patch to configservice/us-east (canary 10%)...
Priya: also seeing 429 rate-limit responses from token-store when bursts happen. Token refresh logic is retrying aggressively causing thundering herd.
Marta: mitigation plan: 1) disable sync FF eval (cache fallback), 2) increase token-store connection pool + add backoff on retries, 3) enable degraded routing to dedicated fallback model variant for streaming clients.
Alex: executing 1 now.
Deploy-Bot: Canary rollout complete (10%). No errors reported.
Alex: moving to 50% rollout.
Infra-Bot: token-store connections dropped from 980 -> 420 after canary. p99 latency of /v1/generate reduced to ~1.6s.
Priya: good sign. But some customers still seeing stalls due to buffered streaming state machines timing out. We'll need to flush queued frames for them.
Jamal: support note: putting guidance for customers to reconnect will work, but we should push server-side immediate reconnect assist.
Taylor: starting step 2: bumping token-store pool size + applying 500ms jittered backoff on refresh worker. Patching now.
Deploy-Bot: token-store manifest updated across controlplane (gradual).
Marta: after pool bump and backoff, connections stable ~300 avg, token-store p99 down to 90ms. System-level p95 back to 300ms, p99 ~1.1s.
Alex: rolling featureflag change to 100%.
Deploy-Bot: FF_EVAL_SYNC=false applied to all configservice pods in us-east.
Priya: verifying traces — flag evaluation latency removed from request path for most traces.
Nina: customer impact update: 14 customers reported degraded streaming experiences, most resolved after reconnect. Two enterprise customers (Acme Pay and Northstar) still have intermittent stalls. Opened high-priority support tickets and informed CSMs.
Lucy: product note: need to assess whether flag evaluation should be sync by default. This is causing customer-visible SLO breaches.
Alex: next immediate action: enable fallback routing — route streaming traffic for customers with tail stalls to a less strict path (model-variant v1-degen) that doesn't do early featureflag checks and uses pre-warmed KV cache. Switching traffic for affected org IDs now.
Taylor: patching routing rules. Adding org-level override for degrade-mode.
Deploy-Bot: Routing updates deployed for orgs: acme-pay, northstar.
Infra-Bot: observe: streaming stalls for those orgs dropped to near-zero. Overall /v1/generate p99 now 0.9s.
Marta: starting post-mortem checklist: collect traces, record deploys, capture rollback window, quantify customer impact (MTTA/MTTR), assign action items.
Priya: I’ll collect distributed traces (jaeger) and sample logs for 14:00-14:20 window.
Jamal: I'll draft the customer status update and coordinate with Nina for ticket replies.
Lucy: product will open a doc to discuss default flag evaluation strategy and rollout gating.
Alex: Ops action items (assigning roughly):
- Alex: orchestrate postmortem writeup and timeline.
- Marta: deep-dive token-store connection pool and circuit-breaker behavior, propose resilience improvements.
- Priya: add tracing and metrics to detect slow featureflag evaluations earlier.
- Taylor: implement exponential backoff in token refreshers and runtime circuit-breaker auto-throttle.
- Jamal/Nina: finalize customer impact notes and CS outreach.
Marta: immediate follow-up: add an alert for token-store connection saturation (threshold 800) and an automated mitigation to reduce token refresh concurrency by 50% if triggered.
Alex: agree. Also add a runbook step to temporarily disable sync featureflag evaluation in case of spike.
Priya: recording retrospective notes: root cause likely a combination of a new featureflag evaluation path (sync), token-store retry storm, and DB connection pool limits — together created cascading backpressure into control-plane and the inference path.
Jamal: preliminary severity: Sev2 (customer impact, degraded but mitigated in <30m for most, but two enterprise customers had longer disruption ~45m).
Nina: tickets updated, customers notified of mitigation steps and committed to post-incident writeup.
Taylor: will also add an integration test that simulates token-store 5xxs to ensure featureflag eval path fails open (cache) within 200ms.
Deploy-Bot: All mitigation patches applied. No further escalations.
Alex: thanks team. Leaving this thread for the postmortem doc. If anything flares up ping me and re-open. :thumbsup:
Marta: filing follow-up tasks in the incidents board now.
Priya: uploading traces & timeline to the doc (link: https://internal.docs/redwood/incidents/2530001234).
Jamal: draft customer status ready for review, pinging Nina.
Nina: ack, I'll send updates.
Oncall-Bot: Incident thread closed by Alex at 2530001876.
